items.pronunciation_notes: The स्क stack runs स straight into क with no vowel between, and the final vowel drops: skuul, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: स्कूल is a school, borrowed from English and keeping its opening cluster intact — unlike गिलास, which had a vowel inserted. It is masculine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable, and the plural does not change. The older word विद्यालय still appears on signboards and in formal writing.

examples.note: बड़ा takes -ा because स्कूल is masculine.
The place comes before the verb.
The masculine adjective ending again.

practice.question: स्कूल
practice.explanation_en: स्कूल is a school. The formal word विद्यालय means the same thing.

game.question_en: राम ___ स्कूल — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: स्कूल is masculine, so का. Its consonant ending gives no clue.

items.pronunciation_notes: The स्प stack sits after the opening vowel, and the word runs to three syllables: aspataal.

learn.explanation_en: अस्पताल is a hospital. It is masculine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable, and the plural does not change. The word came through Portuguese rather than English, which is why it begins with a vowel — a useful one to be able to say clearly, since you may one day need to ask for it in a hurry.

examples.note: The masculine adjective ending.
साफ़ never changes form.
The same pattern as स्कूल जाना.

practice.question: अस्पताल
practice.explanation_en: अस्पताल is a hospital. It is a word worth being able to say clearly.

game.question_en: राम ___ अस्पताल — का, के or की?

items.pronunciation_notes: A short first vowel and a long second one: galii, two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: गली is a narrow lane or alley, the kind that branches off a सड़क and is too small for much traffic. It ends in -ी and is feminine, so the ending predicts correctly, and the plural is गलियाँ. Addresses in older parts of a city are often given by गली rather than by street name.

examples.note: छोटा takes -ी because गली is feminine.
The -ी becomes -ियाँ in the plural.
गंदा also takes -ी here.

practice.question: गली
practice.explanation_en: गली is a narrow lane. सड़क is the wider road it leads off.

game.question_en: राम ___ गली — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: गली is feminine, so की. The -ी ending predicts correctly.

summary.recap_en: This level added स्कूल, अस्पताल and गली. The two borrowed words are masculine and end in consonants, while गली is the one whose ending gives its gender away.
summary.next_up_en: Next: शहर, गाँव and जगह — the city, the village and the general word for a place.

items.pronunciation_notes: The श is the sh of English 'ship', and the final vowel drops: shahar in two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: शहर covers both a city and a decent-sized town, so it is broader than the English word. It is masculine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable, and the plural does not change. You met it in Module 2 as the example word for श.

examples.note: बड़ा takes -ा because शहर is masculine.
Most Indian cities have one, and this is what it is called.
साफ़ never changes form.

practice.question: शहर
practice.explanation_en: शहर is a city or town. गाँव is a village.

game.question_en: राम ___ शहर — का, के or की?

items.pronunciation_notes: The crescent nasalises the vowel and adds no n sound, and the final व is light: gãav, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: गाँव is a village, and it carries a good deal of weight in conversation — most people in India have a गाँव they or their family came from, so the word comes up in introductions constantly. It is masculine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable. The crescent nasalises the vowel without adding any n sound.

examples.note: छोटा takes -ा because गाँव is masculine.
The place comes before the verb.
सुंदर never changes form.

practice.question: गाँव
practice.explanation_en: गाँव is a village. शहर is a city or town.

game.question_en: राम ___ गाँव — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: गाँव is masculine, so का. Its consonant ending predicts nothing.

items.pronunciation_notes: The final ह is lightly pronounced rather than dropped, giving jagah in two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: जगह is a place, and also space in the sense of room for something — जगह है means there is room. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable, and it is worth memorising because it turns up in every kind of sentence. You met it in Module 2 as the example word for ज.

examples.note: अच्छा takes -ी because जगह is feminine.
खाली never changes form, so it hides the gender.
Feminine consonant endings take -एँ.

common_error.why_en: जगह is feminine despite its consonant ending, so the adjective takes -ी.

practice.question: जगह
practice.explanation_en: जगह is a place, and also space or room for something.

game.question_en: राम ___ जगह — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: जगह is feminine, so की. Its consonant ending gives no clue at all.

summary.recap_en: This level covered शहर, गाँव and जगह. All three end in consonants, and जगह is the feminine one — worth fixing in memory, since it appears in more sentences than either of the others.
summary.next_up_en: Next: स्टेशन, मंदिर and इमारत finish the places.

items.pronunciation_notes: The स्ट stack runs स into a retroflex ट, the ए is flat, and the final vowel drops: sṭeshan.

learn.explanation_en: स्टेशन is a railway station, borrowed from English. Notice how the borrowing was reshaped: the t became the retroflex ट, because that is the Hindi sound closest to an English t. It is masculine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable, and the plural does not change.

examples.note: बड़ा takes -ा because स्टेशन is masculine.
The place comes before the verb.
The masculine adjective ending again.

game.question_en: राम ___ स्टेशन — का, के or की?

items.pronunciation_notes: The dot before द is a plain dental n, and the final vowel drops: mandir in two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: मंदिर is a Hindu temple. It is masculine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable, and the plural does not change. The anusvara sits before द, a dental, so it is read as a plain n — compare मंदिर with पंखा, where the dot before ख came out as ng instead.

examples.note: पुराना takes -ा because मंदिर is masculine.
सुंदर never changes form.
The same pattern as स्टेशन जाना.

practice.question: मंदिर
practice.explanation_en: मंदिर is a Hindu temple. मस्जिद is a mosque.

game.question_en: राम ___ मंदिर — का, के or की?

items.pronunciation_notes: The ि matra is drawn before म but read after it, and the final vowel drops: imaarat.

learn.explanation_en: इमारत is a building, usually a substantial one rather than a house. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable. Notice the pattern building up across the places: बाज़ार, स्कूल, अस्पताल, शहर, गाँव, स्टेशन and मंदिर are all masculine, while दुकान, सड़क, गली, जगह and इमारत are feminine. There is no rule behind it.

examples.note: ऊँचा takes -ी because इमारत is feminine.
Feminine consonant endings take -एँ.
पुराना also takes -ी here.

practice.question: इमारत
practice.explanation_en: इमारत is a building. दीवार is a wall within one.

game.question_en: राम ___ इमारत — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: इमारत is feminine, so की. Its consonant ending predicts nothing.

summary.recap_en: This level completed the twelve places. Seven are masculine and five feminine, and eleven of the twelve end in consonants — which is why almost every place word in this module carries a flag.
summary.next_up_en: Next: time words, beginning with the day and the night.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ि matra is drawn before द but read after it, and the final vowel drops: din, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: दिन is a day, both the daylight hours and a full calendar day. It is masculine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable, and the plural does not change. You have met this word repeatedly since Module 1, where it was the example for the short ि matra.

examples.note: अच्छा takes -ा because दिन is masculine.
The masculine adjective ending again.
One masculine, one feminine, both ending in consonants.

practice.question: दिन
practice.explanation_en: दिन is a day. रात is the night that follows it.

game.question_en: राम ___ दिन — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: दिन is masculine, so का. Its consonant ending gives no clue.

items.pronunciation_notes: A single tap for र, a dental त with the tongue on the teeth, and the final vowel drops: raat.

learn.explanation_en: रात is the night. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender has to be learned — and it is worth the effort, because it sits beside दिन in dozens of everyday phrases and the two take opposite forms. Get into the habit of saying ठंडी रात and ठंडा दिन and the pair will stop being a decision.

examples.note: ठंडा takes -ी because रात is feminine.
Compare लंबा दिन, where the same adjective takes -ा.
Feminine consonant endings take -एँ.

common_error.why_en: रात is feminine despite its consonant ending, so the adjective takes -ी.

practice.question: रात
practice.explanation_en: रात is night. शाम is the evening before it.

game.question_en: राम ___ रात — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: रात is feminine, so की — while दिन, also a consonant ending, takes का.

items.pronunciation_notes: The final ह colours the vowel before it rather than sounding separately: subah in two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: सुबह is the morning. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable. The plural सुबहें exists but is rarely needed, since mornings are usually spoken of one at a time. You met the word in Module 2 as an example of the light final ह.

examples.note: अच्छा takes -ी because सुबह is feminine.

examples.english: to get up in the morning
examples.note: The time comes before the verb.
The feminine adjective ending again.

practice.question: सुबह
practice.explanation_en: सुबह is the morning. शाम is the evening.

game.question_en: राम ___ सुबह — का, के or की?

summary.recap_en: This level began the time words with दिन, रात and सुबह. दिन and रात are the pair to fix: both end in consonants, they appear together constantly, and their genders are opposite.

items.pronunciation_notes: The श is the sh of English 'ship', and the final vowel drops: shaam, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: शाम is the evening, the stretch between afternoon and night. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable — though by now the pattern in this section is clear: रात, सुबह and शाम are all feminine, and only दिन is masculine.

examples.note: अच्छा takes -ी because शाम is feminine.
The feminine adjective ending again.
Two feminine nouns, both ending in consonants.

practice.question: शाम
practice.explanation_en: शाम is the evening. रात is the night that follows.

game.question_en: राम ___ शाम — का, के or की?

items.pronunciation_notes: Three syllables with a long middle vowel: mahiinaa.

learn.explanation_en: महीना is a month. It is masculine and ends in -ा, so the gender is predictable and the plural becomes महीने — the first time word in this section whose ending tells you anything. Do not confuse it with महँगा, which is expensive and carries a crescent.

examples.note: पूरा takes -ा because महीना is masculine.
The -ा becomes -े in the plural.
Both masculine, but only one has a helpful ending.

practice.question: महीना
practice.explanation_en: महीना is a month. साल is a year.

game.question_en: राम ___ महीना — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: महीना is masculine, so का. The -ा ending predicts correctly.

items.pronunciation_notes: A clear l at the end, kept bright rather than darkened as English would: saal.

learn.explanation_en: साल is a year. It is masculine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable, and the plural does not change — दो साल is two years, with no ending added. The more formal वर्ष appears in writing and in official language, but साल is what you will hear.

examples.note: पूरा takes -ा because साल is masculine.
The plural is identical to the singular.
नया keeps its य in the masculine singular.

practice.question: साल
practice.explanation_en: साल is a year. The formal word वर्ष means the same thing.

game.question_en: राम ___ साल — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: साल is masculine, so का. Its consonant ending gives no clue.

summary.recap_en: This level added शाम, महीना and साल. Of the six time words so far, only महीना carries an ending that reveals its gender — the other five all have to be memorised.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the last four time words, and then the question words that end the module.
